2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"net"
8		"strings"
9	)
10	
11	// runResolve answers what the target's name maps to, or what its address maps
12	// back to. Exactly one of the two questions has meaning for a given target,
13	// and the other says so rather than being absent.
14	func runResolve(ctx context.Context, t Target, env Env, _ Settings, _ *Results) []Check {
15		if ip := net.ParseIP(strings.TrimSpace(t.Host)); ip != nil {
16			return []Check{
17				literalAddress(ip),
18				reverseLookup(ctx, t, env, ip.String()),
19			}
20		}
21		return []Check{
22			forwardLookup(ctx, t, env),
23			newCheck(CheckReverseDNS, StageResolve, NotApplicable,
24				"Target is a name, not an address"),
25		}
26	}
27	
28	// forwardLookup resolves a name.
29	func forwardLookup(ctx context.Context, t Target, env Env) Check {
30		ips, err := env.Resolve(ctx, t.Host, t.Resolver)
31		c := newCheck(CheckResolve, StageResolve, Fail, "")
32		c.fact("Resolver", resolverLabel(t.Resolver))
33	
34		if err != nil {
35			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s does not resolve", t.Host)
36			c.fact("Error", err.Error())
37			if dnsErr, ok := serverMisbehaved(err); ok {
38				c.Reason = ReasonServerMisbehaving
39				c.fact("Temporary", temporaryLabel(dnsErr.IsTemporary))
40			}
41			return c
42		}
43		if len(ips) == 0 {
44			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s resolves to no address", t.Host)
45			return c
46		}
47	
48		c.Verdict = OK
49		if len(ips) == 1 {
50			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s resolves to %s (%s)", t.Host, ips[0], addressClass(ips[0]))
51		} else {
52			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s resolves to %d addresses", t.Host, len(ips))
53		}
54		for _, ip := range ips {
55			c.fact("Address", fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", ip, addressClass(ip)))
56		}
57		return c
58	}
59	
60	// literalAddress records that no resolution was needed. It is NotApplicable
61	// with no Because: the question has no meaning here, which is a different
62	// thing from having been blocked.
63	func literalAddress(ip net.IP) Check {
64		c := newCheck(CheckResolve, StageResolve, NotApplicable,
65			"Target is a literal address, no resolution needed")
66		c.fact("Address", fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", ip, addressClass(ip)))
67		return c
68	}
69	
70	// reverseLookup asks what an address maps back to.
71	//
72	// A missing PTR record is a Warn and never a Fail: plenty of reachable hosts
73	// have none, and the objective this package serves does not depend on it.
74	func reverseLookup(ctx context.Context, t Target, env Env, ip string) Check {
75		names, err := env.ReverseLookup(ctx, ip, t.Resolver)
76		c := newCheck(CheckReverseDNS, StageResolve, Warn, "")
77		c.fact("Resolver", resolverLabel(t.Resolver))
78	
79		switch {
80		case err != nil:
81			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s has no reverse record", ip)
82			c.fact("Error", err.Error())
83		case len(names) == 0:
84			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s has no reverse record", ip)
85		default:
86			c.Verdict = OK
87			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("%s resolves back to %s", ip, strings.TrimSuffix(names[0], "."))
88			for _, n := range names {
89				c.fact("Name", strings.TrimSuffix(n, "."))
90			}
91		}
92		return c
93	}
94	
95	// resolverLabel names the resolver a lookup used. "System resolver" is not a
96	// placeholder: it is the answer the user cares about, because it is the one
97	// their own traffic will use.
98	func resolverLabel(resolver string) string {
99		if strings.TrimSpace(resolver) == "" {
100			return "System resolver"
101		}
102		return resolver
103	}
104	
105	// serverMisbehaved reports whether err is Go's net.DNSError for a resolver
106	// that answered with something the client could not use — the exact wording
107	// ("server misbehaving") is unexported in net, so this matches the DNSError
108	// field it sets rather than the formatted string, the same way stage_tls.go
109	// matches tls.RecordHeaderError instead of grepping an error message.
110	func serverMisbehaved(err error) (*net.DNSError, bool) {
111		var dnsErr *net.DNSError
112		if errors.As(err, &dnsErr) && dnsErr.Err == "server misbehaving" {
113			return dnsErr, true
114		}
115		return nil, false
116	}
117	
118	// temporaryLabel names the one bit "server misbehaving" leaves out of its own
119	// text: whether the response's code was SERVFAIL (IsTemporary — a transient
120	// problem, worth a retry) or anything else Go's client will not accept
121	// (FORMERR, REFUSED, an unsupported EDNS version...), which does not go away
122	// on its own.
123	func temporaryLabel(temporary bool) string {
124		if temporary {
125			return "Yes — a SERVFAIL response, usually transient"
126		}
127		return "No — the server actively rejected or could not parse the query"
128	}
129	
130	// addressClass names the family an address belongs to.
131	//
132	// The class is what the diagnosis rests on — private or public, routable or
133	// not — never the literal octets. It is also what survives pseudonymisation if
134	// a payload is ever built from these checks.
135	func addressClass(ip net.IP) string {
136		switch {
137		case ip.IsLoopback():
138			return "loopback"
139		case ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast(), ip.IsLinkLocalMulticast():
140			return "link-local"
141		case ip.IsPrivate():
142			return "private"
143		case ip.IsUnspecified():
144			return "unspecified"
145		case ip.To4() == nil:
146			return "public IPv6"
147		default:
148			return "public"
149		}
150	}

1	package netcheck
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"net"
6		"net/url"
7		"strconv"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/netproxy"
10	)
11	
12	// runProxy says whether a proxy variable applies to the target. It observes,
13	// it does not test: nothing is sent to the proxy, nothing is sent anywhere, and
14	// the checks around it stay direct.
15	//
16	// The scheme the HEAD will speak depends on a handshake that runs later, so the
17	// stage asks about both, https first, and merges the answers.
18	func runProxy(_ context.Context, t Target, env Env, _ Settings, _ *Results) []Check {
19		host := net.JoinHostPort(t.Host, strconv.Itoa(t.Port))
20		https := env.ProxyFor(&url.URL{Scheme: "https", Host: host})
21		http := env.ProxyFor(&url.URL{Scheme: "http", Host: host})
22	
23		c := newCheck(CheckProxy, StageProxy, NotApplicable, "")
24		c.fact("HTTPS", describeDecision(https))
25		c.fact("HTTP", describeDecision(http))
26	
27		// A proxy is configured as soon as one scheme is proxied, even when the other
28		// scheme's variable is invalid and the merged verdict says so.
29		c.Proxy = proxyShown(https, http)
30	
31		switch {
32		case https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionInvalid || http.Kind == netproxy.DecisionInvalid:
33			c.Verdict, c.Reason = Warn, ReasonProxyInvalid
34			c.Summary = invalidSummary(https, http)
35		case https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionProxied || http.Kind == netproxy.DecisionProxied:
36			c.Verdict, c.Reason = Info, ReasonProxyConfigured
37			c.Summary = "Configured for this target: " + proxiedSummary(https, http)
38		case https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionExcluded || http.Kind == netproxy.DecisionExcluded:
39			c.Reason, c.Summary = ReasonProxyExcluded, "Excluded by NO_PROXY"
40		case https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionLoopback || http.Kind == netproxy.DecisionLoopback:
41			c.Reason, c.Summary = ReasonProxyLoopback, "Not used for a loopback target"
42		default:
43			c.Reason, c.Summary = ReasonProxyNone, "None"
44		}
45		return []Check{c}
46	}
47	
48	// proxyShown is the proxy a proxied scheme goes through, https first, and empty
49	// when neither scheme is proxied.
50	func proxyShown(https, http netproxy.Decision) string {
51		switch {
52		case https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionProxied:
53			return https.Proxy
54		case http.Kind == netproxy.DecisionProxied:
55			return http.Proxy
56		default:
57			return ""
58		}
59	}
60	
61	// proxyConfigured reads, from the Proxy row already produced, whether a proxy
62	// applies to the target and which one to show. It never reads a Summary.
63	func proxyConfigured(prior *Results) (display string, ok bool) {
64		if prior == nil {
65			return "", false
66		}
67		c, found := prior.Get(CheckProxy)
68		if !found || c.Proxy == "" {
69			return "", false
70		}
71		return c.Proxy, true
72	}
73	
74	// describeDecision is the fact value for one scheme. It names the variable, never
75	// its value: an invalid value is whatever the user typed, and may hold a secret.
76	func describeDecision(d netproxy.Decision) string {
77		switch d.Kind {
78		case netproxy.DecisionProxied:
79			return d.Proxy + " (" + d.Variable + ")"
80		case netproxy.DecisionExcluded:
81			return "excluded by NO_PROXY"
82		case netproxy.DecisionLoopback:
83			return "not used for a loopback target"
84		case netproxy.DecisionInvalid:
85			return "invalid value in " + d.Variable
86		default:
87			return "none"
88		}
89	}
90	
91	func invalidSummary(https, http netproxy.Decision) string {
92		switch {
93		case https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionInvalid && http.Kind == netproxy.DecisionInvalid:
94			return "Invalid " + https.Variable + " and " + http.Variable + " values"
95		case https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionInvalid:
96			return "Invalid " + https.Variable + " value"
97		default:
98			return "Invalid " + http.Variable + " value"
99		}
100	}
101	
102	// proxiedSummary names the proxy, or the two when the schemes differ, and the
103	// one scheme it covers when only one does.
104	func proxiedSummary(https, http netproxy.Decision) string {
105		hs := https.Kind == netproxy.DecisionProxied
106		ps := http.Kind == netproxy.DecisionProxied
107		switch {
108		case hs && ps && https.Proxy == http.Proxy:
109			return https.Proxy
110		case hs && ps:
111			return https.Proxy + " (https), " + http.Proxy + " (http)"
112		case hs:
113			return https.Proxy + " (https only)"
114		default:
115			return http.Proxy + " (http only)"
116		}
117	}
118

2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6	)
7	
8	// runConnect opens a TCP connection to the port the user named.
9	//
10	// This is the check that decides reachability, and it is the stage's gate: if
11	// the port does not answer, there is no handshake to inspect and no response to
12	// read, so TLS and HTTP come back NotApplicable pointing here rather than
13	// producing failures of their own about a connection that never existed.
14	//
15	// The dial is always direct. When it fails and a proxy applies to the target,
16	// the conclusion says so: behind a mandatory proxy a closed direct path is
17	// expected and "does not accept connections" would mislead.
18	func runConnect(ctx context.Context, t Target, env Env, _ Settings, prior *Results) []Check {
19		elapsed, err := env.DialTCP(ctx, t.Addr())
20	
21		c := newCheck(CheckTCP, StageConnect, OK, "")
22		c.fact("Address", t.Addr())
23	
24		if err != nil {
25			c.Verdict = Fail
26			c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("Port %d does not accept connections", t.Port)
27			if display, ok := proxyConfigured(prior); ok {
28				c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf(
29					"Port %d does not accept direct connections; a proxy is configured for this target", t.Port)
30				c.Reason = ReasonDirectFailedProxyConfigured
31				c.fact("Proxy", display)
32			}
33			c.fact("Error", err.Error())
34			return []Check{c}
35		}
36	
37		c.Summary = fmt.Sprintf("Port %d accepted the connection in %s", t.Port, roundedMillis(elapsed))
38		c.fact("Connect time", roundedMillis(elapsed))
39		c.Duration = elapsed
40		return []Check{c}
41	}

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511).** The tests of the Nexus
code (`internal/imagesearch`, `internal/registrymgr`) replay answers measured on
the bench from `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/`, through
`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, no cluster and
no secret. Every fixture is leak-checked in the suite; set
`DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one term per
line) to add names the repository must not carry. A fixture whose Nexus version
differs from `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` fails the suite: regenerate
with `mise run nexus-bench:record`. See `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative

1	// Package netcheck answers one question about one target — is this host
2	// reachable, and is its TLS chain sound — and reports it as a list of checks
3	// carrying verdicts.
4	//
5	// A check is a question that got an answer, not a binary that ran. The
6	// distinction is the point: one handshake produces four checks (chain,
7	// hostname, expiry, version), and reachability is answered by two probes. A
8	// row named after a tool cannot express either, which is why the exit code of
9	// `nc` and the exit code of `curl` used to render as the same red FAIL.
10	//
11	// Nothing here shells out. DNS, ICMP, TCP, TLS and HTTP are answered from this
12	// process, so they answer for the machine DevDesk runs on. The Docker runner
13	// they replaced used --network host, which on Docker Desktop is the
14	// docker-desktop VM's namespace — a different resolver, a different routing
15	// table, and no knowledge of a VPN the user is actually on.
16	package netcheck
17	
18	import (
19		"fmt"
20		"strings"
21		"time"
22	)
23	
24	// Verdict is what a check concluded.
25	//
26	// The zero value is Unknown, deliberately: a check that was never filled in
27	// must not read as a pass. That is the same reasoning behind
28	// scan.Result.SecretVerdict returning a *bool — "nobody looked" displayed as a
29	// clean result is a defect, not a nuance.
30	type Verdict int
31	
32	const (
33		// Unknown means the check could not look. It is not a failure and not a
34		// pass; it is the absence of an observation.
35		Unknown Verdict = iota
36		// NotApplicable means the check has no meaning for this target, or an
37		// upstream failure prevented it. The two are told apart by Check.Because.
38		NotApplicable
39		// OK means the objective is met.
40		OK
41		// Warn means the objective is met but something about it is off.
42		Warn
43		// Fail means the objective is not met.
44		Fail
45		// Info is an observation with no objective to meet, such as which proxy
46		// applies. It is neither good nor bad, so it never colours a headline.
47		Info
48	)
49	
50	// String implements fmt.Stringer. The words are what the UI shows, so they are
51	// English US (Rule 129) and short enough for a table cell.
52	func (v Verdict) String() string {
53		switch v {
54		case NotApplicable:
55			return "N/A"
56		case OK:
57			return "OK"
58		case Warn:
59			return "WARN"
60		case Fail:
61			return "FAIL"
62		case Info:
63			return "INFO"
64		default:
65			return "UNKNOWN"
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// severity ranks verdicts for Summarize. Fail outranks Unknown because a known
70	// failure is more actionable than an absent observation; Unknown outranks Warn
71	// because not having looked is worse than having looked and found a blemish.
72	// NotApplicable and Info rank lowest: they never colour a headline.
73	func (v Verdict) severity() int {
74		switch v {
75		case Fail:
76			return 4
77		case Unknown:
78			return 3
79		case Warn:
80			return 2
81		case OK:
82			return 1
83		default:
84			return 0
85		}
86	}
87	
88	// CheckID identifies one question. It is stable: the explanation table in PR 2
89	// and any serialization are keyed on it.
90	type CheckID string
91	
92	const (
93		CheckResolve      CheckID = "resolve"
94		CheckReverseDNS   CheckID = "reverse-dns"
95		CheckRoute        CheckID = "route"
96		CheckICMP         CheckID = "icmp"
97		CheckProxy        CheckID = "proxy"
98		CheckTCP          CheckID = "tcp"
99		CheckTLSHandshake CheckID = "tls-handshake"
100		CheckTLSChain     CheckID = "tls-chain"
101		CheckTLSHostname  CheckID = "tls-hostname"
102		CheckTLSExpiry    CheckID = "tls-expiry"
103		CheckTLSVersion   CheckID = "tls-version"
104		CheckHTTP         CheckID = "http"
105	)
106	
107	// StageID identifies a layer of the pipeline.
108	type StageID string
109	
110	const (
111		StageResolve StageID = "resolve"
112		StageRoute   StageID = "route"
113		StageReach   StageID = "reach"
114		StageProxy   StageID = "proxy"
115		StageConnect StageID = "connect"
116		StageTLS     StageID = "tls"
117		StageHTTP    StageID = "http"
118	)
119	
120	// Fact is one observed value, shown in a check's detail pane.
121	type Fact struct {
122		Key   string
123		Value string
124	}
125	
126	// Phase is one named, non-overlapping span within a check's Duration — a
127	// waterfall row. Phases are sequential and sum to Duration; a check with
128	// nothing to break down (most of them: one dial, one handshake) leaves this
129	// nil rather than a single phase covering the whole thing, which would say
130	// nothing a bar chart couldn't already say better as a number.
131	type Phase struct {
132		Name     string
133		Duration time.Duration
134	}
135	
136	// Check is one answered question.
137	type Check struct {
138		ID      CheckID
139		Stage   StageID
140		Title   string
141		Verdict Verdict
142		// Summary is the one line the results table shows. It states what was
143		// observed, never what to do about it — the advice belongs to the
144		// explanation layer, which is keyed on ID.
145		Summary string
146		Facts   []Fact
147		// Duration is how long the observation behind this check took, when
148		// timed. Zero means untimed — a check that answers instantly (DNS
149		// resolution) or one nothing has instrumented yet.
150		Duration time.Duration
151		// Phases breaks Duration down into a waterfall, when there is more than
152		// one span worth showing separately (today: the HTTP check's DNS,
153		// connect, TLS, server wait and content transfer). Nil elsewhere.
154		Phases []Phase
155		// Because is set only when Verdict is NotApplicable *and* the cause was an
156		// upstream failure. Empty on a NotApplicable that simply has no meaning
157		// here, which is what separates "blocked" from "irrelevant".
158		Because CheckID
159		// Reason is a stable sub-code for a verdict that has more than one cause.
160		//
161		// It exists because the remedies differ where the verdict does not: a chain
162		// that fails because the leaf is self-signed, because the server sent no
163		// intermediates, and because the root is unknown are one Fail with three
164		// different things to go and do. Summary already says which in prose;
165		// Reason is what an explanation — or a serialization — can switch on.
166		//
167		// Empty is the common case: most verdicts have exactly one cause.
168		Reason Reason
169		// Routes is set on CheckRoute only: one lookup per address asked, in the
170		// order asked. Nil on a placeholder (skipped or cancelled stage). It holds
171		// raw errors and is never shown nor serialized.
172		Routes []RouteLookup
173		// Proxy is set on CheckProxy only, when at least one scheme is proxied: the
174		// redacted proxy as shown, https first. It lets the connect stage tell that a
175		// proxy applies without parsing a Summary. It is never shown nor serialized.
176		Proxy string
177	}
178	
179	// Reason discriminates the causes of a verdict that has several. It is stable:
180	// the guidance table is keyed on it.
181	type Reason string
182	
183	const (
184		// DNS resolution
185		//
186		// "Server misbehaving" is Go's net.DNSError wording for a resolver that
187		// answered but with something the client could not use — not a timeout,
188		// not NXDOMAIN. It is worth telling apart because the remedy is neither
189		// "check the spelling" nor "check the network": it is almost always the
190		// resolver itself, commonly a router's built-in DNS proxy choking on the
191		// EDNS0 queries Go's resolver sends (which this pipeline must use to
192		// reach a resolver the user names — see resolverFor in env.go).
193		ReasonServerMisbehaving Reason = "server-misbehaving"
194	
195		// Certificate chain
196		ReasonSelfSigned      Reason = "self-signed"
197		ReasonNoIntermediates Reason = "no-intermediates"
198		ReasonUntrustedRoot   Reason = "untrusted-root"
199		ReasonChainIncomplete Reason = "chain-incomplete"
200	
201		// Certificate validity
202		ReasonExpired     Reason = "expired"
203		ReasonNotYetValid Reason = "not-yet-valid"
204	
205		// ICMP
206		ReasonNoReply     Reason = "no-reply"
207		ReasonPartialLoss Reason = "partial-loss"
208	
209		// TLS handshake
210		ReasonNotTLS Reason = "not-tls"
211	
212		// Local route
213		ReasonPartialRoute      Reason = "partial-route"
214		ReasonRouteUndetermined Reason = "route-undetermined"
215	
216		// Proxy
217		ReasonProxyNone       Reason = "proxy-none"
218		ReasonProxyConfigured Reason = "proxy-configured"
219		ReasonProxyExcluded   Reason = "proxy-excluded"
220		ReasonProxyLoopback   Reason = "proxy-loopback"
221		ReasonProxyInvalid    Reason = "proxy-invalid"
222	
223		// TCP connect
224		ReasonDirectFailedProxyConfigured Reason = "direct-failed-proxy-configured"
225	)
226	
227	// fact appends an observed value, skipping empty ones so a detail pane never
228	// shows a key with nothing beside it.
229	func (c *Check) fact(key, value string) {
230		if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
231			return
232		}
233		c.Facts = append(c.Facts, Fact{Key: key, Value: value})
234	}
235	
236	// Target is what is being checked.
237	type Target struct {
238		Host string
239		Port int
240		// Resolver is the nameserver to query, "host" or "host:port". Empty means
241		// the system resolver — which is the answer the user actually cares about,
242		// so it is the default rather than a fallback.
243		Resolver string
244	}
245	
246	// Addr returns the host:port form used to dial.
247	func (t Target) Addr() string {
248		return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", t.Host, t.Port)
249	}
250	
251	// Validate rejects a target the stages cannot act on. The view validates too,
252	// but this is a package boundary and external data is not trusted at one.
253	func (t Target) Validate() error {
254		if strings.TrimSpace(t.Host) == "" {
255			return fmt.Errorf("target is required")
256		}
257		if t.Port < 1 || t.Port > 65535 {
258			return fmt.Errorf("port must be a number between 1 and 65535")
259		}
260		return nil
261	}
262	
263	// Results holds the checks a run produced, in pipeline order.
264	//
265	// It is a type rather than a []Check because a stage needs to read what came
266	// before it — the HTTP stage picks its scheme from the handshake's outcome —
267	// and because the order is meaningful and must not be re-derived by a caller.
268	type Results struct {
269		checks []Check
270		index  map[CheckID]int
271	}
272	
273	func (r *Results) add(c Check) {
274		if r.index == nil {
275			r.index = make(map[CheckID]int)
276		}
277		if i, ok := r.index[c.ID]; ok {
278			r.checks[i] = c
279			return
280		}
281		r.index[c.ID] = len(r.checks)
282		r.checks = append(r.checks, c)
283	}
284	
285	// clone returns a deep-enough copy: the slice and the index are fresh, so
286	// adding to the copy cannot write into the original's backing array. It is what
287	// makes RunStep safe to call on a goroutine while the caller still holds the
288	// previous value.
289	func (r Results) clone() Results {
290		out := Results{
291			checks: make([]Check, len(r.checks)),
292			index:  make(map[CheckID]int, len(r.index)),
293		}
294		copy(out.checks, r.checks)
295		for k, v := range r.index {
296			out.index[k] = v
297		}

1	// Package netcheck answers one question about one target — is this host
2	// reachable, and is its TLS chain sound — and reports it as a list of checks
3	// carrying verdicts.
4	//
5	// A check is a question that got an answer, not a binary that ran. The
6	// distinction is the point: one handshake produces four checks (chain,
7	// hostname, expiry, version), and reachability is answered by two probes. A
8	// row named after a tool cannot express either, which is why the exit code of
9	// `nc` and the exit code of `curl` used to render as the same red FAIL.
10	//
11	// Nothing here shells out. DNS, ICMP, TCP, TLS and HTTP are answered from this
12	// process, so they answer for the machine DevDesk runs on. The Docker runner
13	// they replaced used --network host, which on Docker Desktop is the
14	// docker-desktop VM's namespace — a different resolver, a different routing
15	// table, and no knowledge of a VPN the user is actually on.
16	package netcheck
17	
18	import (
19		"fmt"
20		"strings"
21		"time"
22	)
23	
24	// Verdict is what a check concluded.
25	//
26	// The zero value is Unknown, deliberately: a check that was never filled in
27	// must not read as a pass. That is the same reasoning behind
28	// scan.Result.SecretVerdict returning a *bool — "nobody looked" displayed as a
29	// clean result is a defect, not a nuance.
30	type Verdict int
31	
32	const (
33		// Unknown means the check could not look. It is not a failure and not a
34		// pass; it is the absence of an observation.
35		Unknown Verdict = iota
36		// NotApplicable means the check has no meaning for this target, or an
37		// upstream failure prevented it. The two are told apart by Check.Because.
38		NotApplicable
39		// OK means the objective is met.
40		OK
41		// Warn means the objective is met but something about it is off.
42		Warn
43		// Fail means the objective is not met.
44		Fail
45		// Info is an observation with no objective to meet, such as which proxy
46		// applies. It is neither good nor bad, so it never colours a headline.
47		Info
48	)
49	
50	// String implements fmt.Stringer. The words are what the UI shows, so they are
51	// English US (Rule 129) and short enough for a table cell.
52	func (v Verdict) String() string {
53		switch v {
54		case NotApplicable:
55			return "N/A"
56		case OK:
57			return "OK"
58		case Warn:
59			return "WARN"
60		case Fail:
61			return "FAIL"
62		case Info:
63			return "INFO"
64		default:
65			return "UNKNOWN"
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// severity ranks verdicts for Summarize. Fail outranks Unknown because a known
70	// failure is more actionable than an absent observation; Unknown outranks Warn
71	// because not having looked is worse than having looked and found a blemish.
72	// NotApplicable and Info rank lowest: they never colour a headline.
73	func (v Verdict) severity() int {
74		switch v {
75		case Fail:
76			return 4
77		case Unknown:
78			return 3
79		case Warn:
80			return 2
81		case OK:
82			return 1
83		default:
84			return 0
85		}
86	}

174		// redacted proxy as shown, https first. It lets the connect stage tell that a

203		ReasonNotYetValid Reason = "not-yet-valid"
204	
205		// ICMP

207		ReasonPartialLoss Reason = "partial-loss"
208

211

Phase ROUGE de DEVDESK-604 : les tests sont écrits, ils compilent, et 15 tests échouent par assertion (aucun panic). Je n'ai rien commité.

**Squelette de prod ajouté (inévitable, sans comportement)**
- `internal/netcheck/netcheck.go` : constante `ReasonDirectResolveFailedProxyConfigured = "direct-resolve-failed-proxy-configured"`.
- `internal/netcheck/run.go` : champs `amends []CheckID` et `conclude func(t Target, res *Results)` dans `stage`. Ils ne sont ni renseignés dans `stages()` ni appelés par `runStage`.
- `internal/netcheck/stage_resolve.go` : `func concludeResolveBehindProxy(_ Target, _ *Results) {}`, vide.
- Je n'ai pas ajouté `withFactAfter`, aucun test ne l'appelle directement. Il reste à écrire avec le code de prod.

**Tests**
- `internal/netcheck/stage_resolve_proxy_test.go` (nouveau) contient tous les tests de la liste, sauf le dernier qui est dans `run_test.go`. J'y ai ajouté `TestTheConclusionNeedsItsPremises`, qui appelle `concludeResolveBehindProxy` directement.
